ruling.reasoning:
SAFETY SCREEN: the only chat message is a route question ("mind if I go round via Zion Road?"); the driver's statement and the rider's complaint contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

THE TRIP. RydeTAXI, metered. Quoted route 7.726 km / 16.5 min; fare shows distance_km 13.03 and time_min 28.33, i.e. ~5.3 km more than the quote. Request 18:20:35, pickup 18:27:00, dropoff 18:55:45 (28.75 min). The GPS trace (5 s → 30 s thinned) shows two unexplained departures from the quoted polyline.

Segment 1 (18:27:10–18:28:10): the trace runs Clarke Quay → (1.2925,103.8444) → back through (1.2913,103.8461) → (1.2902,103.8479). That is literally the quoted polyline driven out and back along the same points — a U-turn with no stop: extra_km ≈ 2×(out-and-back distance) ≈ 1.2 km. No incident on the replaced portion; no rider message before it (the sole chat message is at 18:30:30, after this loop ended). The driver's "no objection so I took it" is not consent (G11) and cannot reach a loop that was over before the question existed. Ground = consent_after_or_none (driver_errand overlap) → counts.

Segment 2 (≈18:31–18:45, Zion Road / Havelock / Tiong Bahru / Bukit Merah corridor): the chat message at 18:30:30 names Zion Road and the timing fits the start of the diverging segment; the replacement for the Kampong Bahru Road stretch of the quoted route (band 2, slow, 18:16–18:34) is a plausible traffic-driven alternative, but the trace dips as far as ~1.2699 N / 103.823 E in the River Valley–Zion area and none of the trace points lie on Zion Road itself, and it does not rejoin the quoted corridor until ~18:46 at River Valley Road. Because the record names a road the driver offered but does not tie the actually driven path to that road (indeed places the drive elsewhere), the agreement cannot supply an exemption that covers this segment; the divergence is ~3.8–4.1 km of extra driving. Ground = named_road_untied/elsewhere → undetermined.

METERED REFUND (RD-2). Rate = distance_fare / distance_km = 18.37 / 13.03 = $1.4098/km. Smallest defensible amount, counting only segment 1 (the out-and-back) as clearly unexempt: 1.2 km × $1.4098 = $1.69. If segment 2 is also held to count, the refund would be ≈ (1.2+4.0) × 1.4098 ≈ $7.33. Waiting element ($0.11 meter waiting) is not refundable as mileage and is separately de minimis/no rider cost beyond the meter.

CONSEQUENCE. The finding on segment 2 changes the amount by ~$5.6, so an escalation is required on that element, and the driver has no upheld route dispute in 90 days (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0), so neither RD-6 nor NS-2 triggers a flag; any account marking flows from the automated gate — do not write flag_account in the ruling. Escalate with the quantified computation for human confirmation; if the reviewer adopts only segment 1, the refund is $1.69 (refund_partial) and no account flag.
ruling.escalation_reason: The off-route segment on the named-road element (Zion Road corridor) is undetermined under RD-5 + G13 — the record names a road but does not tie the driven path to it — and resolving it changes the refund from $1.69 to ≈$7.33; the driver's errand loop and its quantified 1.2 km override are submitted with it.

No LTA incident exists (traffic.incidents empty), and speed band 2 alone does not exempt a segment (RD-4(b), MVP). Band 2 also sits on the original Kampong Bahru Road stretch, not on the Zion Road loop, so it cannot exempt the earlier loop.
